analysis:
Examined the waitlist gating added in this PR: runOnboarding in ClusterSetupWizardCommand.swift (head line 116 calls requireNewPairApproval, defined at 151-154), the Waitlist.self subcommand registration (Darkbloom.swift head line 60) and the Sandbox help text (SandboxCommand.swift head lines 28-31). The Sandbox setup command patch (SandboxSetupCommand.swift) was visible only as a truncated excerpt with no numbered text, so I could not inspect its gating logic.

Security view: the waitlist gate is a client-side product/eligibility check that runs before onboarding for a Mac with no pairing. It sits outside the provider wire and custody boundaries (TB-002, TB-011) and the TB-013 installer path. It adds no new trust in coordinator-signed authorization, no serving authorization (A-016) and no attestation material. It only adds early refusal, so it cannot weaken existing controls. A Mac that already holds a pairing skips the gate by design (`guard !pair.paired`). That is a documented backward-compatibility choice and not a bypass of any threat-model security control. The gate is a UX or eligibility control, not an authorization boundary. The real enforcement of cluster or sandbox access must live on the coordinator or sandbox service, which is outside the supplied evidence.

Open questions for deeper review: (1) the FeatureWaitlistAccess.live and FeatureWaitlistGate implementation, including which URL and credential it uses, TLS enforcement, how it fails on a network error or unreadable state (fail-open or fail-closed), and whether it sends the provider token (A-008) to the right host; (2) the new Waitlist subcommand, which was not supplied and which may call the coordinator with an account token; (3) the sandbox setup gate (TB-013, T-061) at lines 164-185 and 277-295, and whether it runs before the installer download and execution. These could not be verified, so I record them as unverified contracts and not as findings.
